Hi Asha / Raman —

Thanks again for the demo call this morning. Quick recap from our side and the concrete next steps we agreed on: 

Summary of needs (from call):
- Target p95 latency: 250ms for single-item streaming responses (customer chat flows).
- Peak throughput target: ~1,200 qps sustained (B2B peak hours), concurrency bursts to 3k qps for short windows.
- Concurrent sessions: typically 5–10k active sessions with mostly short prompts (~150 tokens).
- Streaming required for first-byte latency & progressive answer rendering.
- SLOs: 99.9% availability, p95 latency <= 250ms for streaming responses, and cost goal ~ $0.003 / 1k tokens (ballpark).

Open questions we noted:
1) What percent of your traffic needs strict streaming (first byte within 100ms) vs. non-streaming?
2) Typical sequence length distributions (tokens): median, 90th, 95th.
3) Tolerance for model quantization / quality delta on a small subset of prompts (we can quantify tradeoffs).

What we'll send today:
- A short SLO workbook (attached) for you to drop in observed token distributions and concurrency patterns.
- A recommended set of cost/performance levers we discussed (batching, KV caching, quantization profiles, model variants) and estimated impact ranges based on similar customers.

Next steps / asks:
- Asha / Raman: drop the token distribution + % streaming rows into the attached workbook and share by EOD Tuesday.
- Rishi / I will run a quick sizing + cost sensitivity (dedicated vs hosted) and share recommended config options by Wednesday.
- Book follow-up for Thu 4/8 to review numbers and runway.

Attachments: Orchid_SLO_Workbook_v1.xlsx (workbook), redwood-performance-profiles.pdf (short primer).

Great — thanks for the numbers, Asha. Attached is a quick note + estimated impact ranges using those distributions. High-level guidance below (we'll put exact numbers into the workbook after you populate it):

1) Continuous batching (lower-latency batching)
- Use small dynamic batch windows for streaming head requests (20–60ms windows) to preserve first-byte latency while aggregating tokens for backend throughput. Expected p95 latency impact: +10–30ms; cost reduction: 5–15% depending on traffic burstiness.

2) KV / prefix caching
- Cache recent session prefixes (100–500 tokens) for repeat-turn chats. For your 6k active sessions, a small KV cache reduces total token compute by ~18–25% for chat-heavy flows. Improves p95 latency because cached prefixes avoid recomputation.

3) Quantization profiles and model variants
- Offer tiered model variants: FP16-optimized baseline for highest quality, int8/4 quantized variants for cost-sensitive traffic. Based on our benchmarks: int8 yields ~30–40% reduction in per-token GPU cost with <2% quality delta on short prompts; int4/4x aggressive quantization saves more but needs evaluation on your eval set.

4) Model-selection routing + graceful fallback
- Route low-latency-critical traffic to smaller, faster model variants pinned to dedicated capacity. Route non-critical batch jobs to cheaper, highly-quantized instances. Automatic fallback if capacity limits hit. Expected availability + reliability improvement during bursts.

5) Dedicated capacity vs hosted (burst) mix
- For sustained 1,200 qps and burst to 3k qps, a hybrid approach looks promising: reserved dedicated pool sized to cover ~1.2k sustained with autoscaling policies + hosted burst capacity for peak events. This reduces committed spend while keeping headroom.

Next steps from us: Rishi and I will produce a short cost sensitivity table (dedicated vs hosted) and fill the workbook with sample numbers by Wed. Can you confirm a Thurs slot (4/8) 10:00–10:30am PT to review?

Attachments: redwood-performance-profiles.pdf (same primer).

Thanks,
Marissa
